, in our opinion, there is no convincing evidence that RBC osmotic lability in chronic renal failure is due to secondary HPT, at least as long as the latter is not very severe, and that the effect of the treatment with l, 25-(OH) 2D 3 is not related to the control of secondary HPT.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the osmotic fragili-ty of erythrocyte is not a good marker for secondary HPT in chronic renal failure, at least in the patients we studied.
we found no correlation between RBC fragility and serum levels of PTH.

The main takeaway from our work is that
we can’t just rely on a single test to diagnose a condition.
